Benito Mussolini. The founder of Italian fascism and the dictatorial leader of Italy from nineteen twenty-two until his fall in nineteen forty-three. Rising to power as a firebrand nationalist, Mussolini transformed Italy into a totalitarian fascist state, pursued aggressive imperial expansion in Africa and the Mediterranean, and led Italy as an Axis power alongside Nazi Germany during World War Two. His grandiose vision of reviving a Roman Empire ended in military disaster, occupation, and his own execution by Italian partisans in nineteen forty-five.

Mussolini was born in Romagna in eighteen eighty-three. He began as a socialist journalist before embracing violent nationalism during World War One. In nineteen nineteen, he founded the Fasci Italiani di Combattimento, the Italian Combat Squad, a paramilitary organization that became the nucleus of fascism. These black-shirted squads intimidated opponents and seized power through violence and intimidation.

Mussolini became Prime Minister in nineteen twenty-two after the March on Rome, a paramilitary demonstration of force that forced King Victor Emmanuel the Third to invite him to lead the government. Throughout the nineteen twenties, he consolidated dictatorial power by eliminating parliamentary democracy, suppressing opposition parties and the press, and declaring himself Il Duce, the Leader.

He invaded Abyssinia, also called Ethiopia, in nineteen thirty-five and Albania in nineteen thirty-nine. These conquests drew Italy closer to Nazi Germany, eventually forming the Axis alliance in nineteen thirty-six, known as the Rome-Berlin Axis. Mussolini entered World War Two in nineteen forty on Germany's side, expecting a quick victory. Military failures in North Africa and the Mediterranean forced increasing dependence on German military support.

He fell from power in July nineteen forty-three after military defeats and internal political betrayal. German commandos rescued him and established a puppet fascist republic in northern Italy under German protection. In April nineteen forty-five, Italian partisans captured and executed Mussolini alongside his mistress. His body was displayed publicly and mutilated in revenge.
